sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Rajvendra Singh,Vikash Kumar Maurya
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Rateesh Singh
Hon'ble Vivek Varma,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed by counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri V.P. Tripathi, learned AGA for the State, Sri Rateesh Singh, counsel for the informant and perused the material on record.
3.
This application has been filed seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 68 of 2024, under sections 498A, 323, 376, 506 of I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of D.P., Police Station Rehad, District- Bijnor.
4. Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the instant case.
The applicant is the brother-in-law of the informant.
A matrimonial dispute exists between the parties.
The allegation of rape has been levelled against the applicant on 13.12.2023.

The first Shivam Kumar @ Ranjeet vs State Of U.P. on 5 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147787504/

sentences.text: The delay is fatal to the prosecution case.

Prior to the lodging of the first information report, the informant had filed an application before Mahila Thana,
Moradabad dated 13.12.2023 and had also filed a complaint under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the applicant and others.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
In the said application,
there is no allegation of rape against the applicant.
In such circumstances, it is contended that the instant case is an afterthought.
It is next contended that after investigation, the Police submitted a final report in favour of the applicant.
Subsequent, thereto, the informant submitted an application before the Superintendent of Police, Bijnor.
Pursuant, thereto, the investigation has again started.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents.
It is next submitted that the investigation is going on and the applicant has apprehension of his arrest in the above mentioned case.
5. Learned A.G.A. and counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail but could not satisfactorily dispute the aforesaid submissions from the record.

6. Having regard to the submissions made by counsel for the applicant, considering the nature of accusations, antecedents of the applicant and the fact that the F.I.R. was lodged belatedly, the fact that there is no allegation of rape against the applicant in the application before Mahila Thana,
Mordabad dated 13.12.2023 and in the complaint under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, without commenting on merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

(vi) In case, the applicant misuse the liberty of bail, the Court concerned may take appropriate action in accordance with law and judgment of Apex Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal vs. State (NCT of Delhi) 2020 SCC Online SC 98;
(vii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 351 of B.N.S.S.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal vs. State (NCT of Delhi) 2020 SCC Online SC 98
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If in the opinion of the trial court default of this condition is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of his bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
8. In default of any of the conditions, the court concerned is at liberty to pass appropriate orders for enforcing and compelling the same.

9. The application stands disposed of.
